subject.title: [Feature]: Add user-visible and confirmable context compaction mechanisms

question: Should OpenClaw add a core pre-apply compaction preview and user confirmation/rollback contract, or should the current notices/checkpoints/hooks remain the supported transparency surface for now?
rationale: The remaining request changes user-visible compaction behavior, public config, transcript retention, and security boundaries, so automation cannot choose the product and privacy contract safely.

options.title: Design core contract first
options.body: Specify UX, permissions, redaction, retention, defaults, and migration behavior before adding preview, approval, modification, or rollback controls.

options.title: Narrow to existing surfaces
options.body: Treat notifyUser, compaction hooks, checkpoints, and branch/restore as the supported transparency model and split only concrete bugs into narrower issues.

options.title: Move extensibility to plugins
options.body: Keep core limited to generic hooks/checkpoints and require custom preview or compaction strategy behavior to use plugin APIs unless a missing core API is proven.

recommendation.title: Design core contract first
recommendation.body: Specify UX, permissions, redaction, retention, defaults, and migration behavior before adding preview, approval, modification, or rollback controls.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the visible compaction/resume work and is a reasonable routing candidate for the product-level decision on expanding that surface.
